children: Asian stocks fell on Tuesday November 17, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street as investors stayed wary of the AI trade ahead of Nvidia's much-awaited earnings and Anthropic PBC's expected market debut.
The MSCI Asia Pacific Index slipped 0.7% in early trading, while South Korea's Kospi lost 1.92%. Japan's Nikkei 225 shed 1.03% and the broader Topix dropped 1.30%.
In Japan, former Bank of Japan Governor Haruhiko Kuroda told Bloomberg that rates may have to rise above the neutral level if inflation worsens, citing price pressure from Trump's war with Iran.

In India, GIFT Nifty pointed to a muted, slightly positive start for the weekly options expiry session. Falling oil supports sentiment, though the AI sell-off could spill over from Asia. The Nifty finds strong support at 25,150-25,200, while the Nifty Bank, less than 200 points from its record high, has a buffer at 61,200-61,000.

US Treasuries rose on Monday, and a gauge of the dollar edged higher before holding steady on Tuesday. The Japanese yen was little changed at 159.42 per dollar, while the offshore yuan stayed near 6.6641.

Futures on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 barely moved after the underlying benchmarks tumbled 1.9% and 2.7% respectively on Monday, their third straight session of losses. The Dow Jones and Nasdaq 100 each fell about 750 points, and the Nasdaq Composite ended 2.5% lower. A gauge of US chip stocks sank 5.3%.

Nvidia led the retreat as its shares dropped 4.1% on Monday and now stand nearly 35% below their peak, pushing its market capitalisation under $4 trillion. The slide followed the stock's worst week since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump's sweeping tariffs rattled global markets.

Investors now seem to face two major concerns regarding the AI sector. Nvidia reports results after the US market close on Tuesday, which will show how strong chip demand is and how the company copes with Jensen Huang's exit. CNBC reported, citing a source, that Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back and remains focused on a national security investigation. Trump, however, backed calls for his reinstatement, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded a "dramatic" leadership shakeup.

Anthropic's listing is the second test, that investors may remain focused upon after Bloomberg reported that demand has reached about seven times the shares on offer. Bankers expect to price the IPO on Wednesday, with trading starting Thursday, in what could be the largest first-time share sale ever, the report said.

The US Commerce Department, meanwhile, released an interim rule requiring data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia to obtain a licence before buying advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other American makers. Washington seems to have come about with this requirement as it wants to stop Chinese firms such as Alibaba Group Holding and Bytedance from accessing the chips remotely through the region's data centres.
The Financial Times reported that Washington and its allies agreed to protect AI technologies and supply chains they see as vulnerable to China.

US Fed Chair Kevin Warsh also unsettled markets on Monday after he avoided monetary policy but warned that a disappointing AI trade could trigger a steep fall in equities and an economic slowdown, with unemployment rising more sharply. Meanwhile, Fed officials signalled another rate rise is likely in December, and futures price a hike then and another in January.

Oil prices meanwhile, fell sharply as Brent crude dropped 4% overnight to near $90 a barrel after several global investment banks warned of a market surplus by 2027, as West Asian exports grow faster than demand. Goldman Sachs expects a "sizeable" surplus, with Brent averaging $88 a barrel next year and falling to $78 by December.

title: Kospi slumps nearly 2%; Asian markets fall as AI sell-off deepens ahead of Nvidia results, Anthropic IPO
